title: A finite union of sets D(f) ∩ V(g_1,…,g_n) in an affine spectrum is a finite disjoint union of such sets
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $\operatorname{Spec}A$ its spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Call a subset of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ *basic* if it is of the form $D(f)\cap V(g_1,\dots,g_n)$ with $f,g_1,\dots,g_n\in A$, $n\ge0$, where $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p:f\notin\mathfrak p\}$ and $V(g_1,\dots,g_n)=\{\mathfrak p:g_1,\dots,g_n\in\mathfrak p\}$. If $B_1,\dots,B_m\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$ ($m\ge0$) are basic, then there are finitely many basic subsets $C_1,\dots,C_p\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$ ($p\ge0$), pairwise disjoint, with $B_1\cup\dots\cup B_m=C_1\cup\dots\cup C_p$.

proof.text: Let basics be the range of BasicConstructibleSetData.toSet. It contains the empty set, represented by f = 0 and no closed generators. The intersection of the basic data P and Q is represented by f = P.f * Q.f and the concatenation of their closed generators: membership follows from primality and membership in both lists. For two members, use [lem-weil-pbc-affine-basic-set-difference] and take the finite image of its indexed pieces under toSet. Distinct sets in that image come from distinct indices, so pairwise disjointness descends to the image; its union is the difference. These constructions prove MeasureTheory.IsSetSemiring basics.

Take the finite image J of the input family under toSet. Apply Mathlib MeasureTheory.IsSetSemiring.disjointOfUnion_props (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/SetSemiring.lean) to J and the semiring proof. It supplies a finite family K(s) of basic sets for each s in J such that all members of their finite union Q = J.biUnion K are pairwise disjoint and the union of Q equals the union of J. This is Mathlib's already-proved finite disjointization argument, replacing the hand-written nested induction below the unit level.

For each member q of Q choose basic data D(q) whose toSet is q, using membership of K(s) in basics. Index Q by Fin Q.card with Q.equivFin.symm and use C(i) = D(Q.equivFin.symm i). Injectivity of this equivalence and of subtype coercion transfers pairwise disjointness to the indices. Surjectivity transfers the union equality to the required indexed union. Finite images permit duplicate or empty input sets; when m = 0, J and Q are empty and p = 0, so the empty-family case also holds.
